findings.title: Night and day as a differentiated, usable order
findings.claim: By effacing the night sign and making the day sign sight-giving, the focus gives the pair distinct functions through which years can be counted and bounty sought. The wider parallels in 10:5 and 28:73 extend those uses, while 73:20 bounds any claim of exhaustive human measure.
findings.mechanism: The focus contrasts the erased night sign with the sight-giving day sign, then names seeking the Lord's bounty, knowing the number of years and reckoning, and detailing everything. In 10:67 night is again paired with rest and day with visibility; 10:5 joins luminaries and measured stations to counted years, calculation, and detailed signs. In 28:73 the night/day pair is tied to rest and seeking bounty, while 73:20 places measured night and day beside a stated human limit on enumerating the night vigil. These contacts turn the paired signs into a wider pattern of perceptual, economic, and calendrical use, without making that measure exhaustive.
findings.reader_payoff: The pair reads as a practical order for seeking provision and reckoning time, while the night-vigil counterpoint keeps countable years from implying complete human command of every temporal measure.
findings.containment: This resonance leaves the focus's direct sequence intact: two signs, the night sign effaced, the day sign made sight-giving, bounty sought, years counted, reckoning known, and everything detailed. The limit in 73:20 concerns the described night vigil and does not cancel the focus's calendrical count; none of the wider links identifies the physical effect of erasing the night sign.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The day-sign's visibility is one functional half of an ordered temporal pair.

branch_activations.boundary: This is a secondary cross-root resonance, not a replacement gloss for مُبْصِرَةً; the Form IV sight-giving form remains explicit.
